notes: Case concerns a lease renewal option, partnership dissolution among joint lessees of a skating rink, and admissibility of evidence of tenant misconduct in a trespass/eviction suit against an unincorporated market association; no bearing on lodging or boarding.

holding_summary: A decedent who had boarded for many years with a household family, paying $20/month until agreeing to defer payment pending recovery of bank stock pledged as collateral, left an estate liable for nineteen months' accrued board at $20/month. The court held the ordinary presumption that board is paid periodically was rebutted by direct testimony of the parties' deferral agreement, and allowed the claim subject to a setoff for the rental value of a house the claimant's family occupied rent-free during the same period.

quotes.text: A claim against an estate of a decedent for nineteen months’ boarding at $20.00 per month should be allowed, where the evidence shows that the decedent had boarded with the claimant for many years, and had regularly paid her $20.00 per month until nineteen months before his death;

The decedent, William C. Martin, had resided for a long term of years with the family of the appellant, Mary L. Moorhead, and there is evidence that he had been paying for his boarding $20.00 per month.

We think the testimony was sufficient to establish the fact that the decedent boarded with the appellant during the period above stated under an agreement to pay $20.00 per month to the appellant and that the evidence overcame the presumption of periodical payments, such as are usually made under the circumstances.

notes: Actual boarding relationship spanned 'many years' / 'a long term of years'; duration_of_occupancy set to 'months' as the closest enum value to the litigated 19-month period, though the underlying occupancy predated that by years.
Dispute over whether a subtenant corporation (House of Refuge) verbally agreed to a new year-to-year sublease versus its written sixty-days-notice lease; no lodging/boarding issue.
Landlord's distraint on a stranger's soda-fountain apparatus for tenant's rent, and whether the equipment lease was a bailment or conditional sale; unrelated to lodging/boarding.

Suit by hotel landlords against a tenant's sureties after tenant abandoned the premises for failure to repair heating; 'boarders would not stay and transient guests would not patronize the hotel' is cited only as evidence of the hotel's lost business, not as a holding on the legal character of lodging/boarding.

Physician-office tenants sued landlord for breach of implied covenant of quiet enjoyment after she leased the rest of the building to a hotel/bar operator; addresses scope of the quiet-enjoyment covenant, not the legality or regulation of letting rooms or boarding.
Equity suit over coal mining waste under an 1821 agricultural lease and use of mine passageways; no lodging/boarding issue.

Will-construction dispute over whether a life-estate devise of 'the premises occupied by me' to testator's housekeeper included a portion of the building rented to a bank as tenant; concerns testamentary construction of 'occupied,' not letting/boarding law.

Statutory proceeding to frame an ejectment issue over possession of a two-acre lot with several dwellings; tenants' rent payments are discussed only as evidence of adverse possession, not as a lodging/boarding holding.
Dispute over whether a tenant's rent payment to the landlord's wife (co-owner by entireties) satisfied the lease obligation; concerns tenancy-by-entireties property law, not lodging/boarding.

Prohibition-era liquor confiscation/search-warrant case construing 'private dwelling' under the Snyder Act; 'boarding house' appears only as one entry in a list of business uses (store, shop, saloon, restaurant, hotel, boarding house, warehouse, public garage) that strip a dwelling of search protection — dicta about liquor search law, not a holding on lodging/boarding regulation.
Commercial lease abandonment/surrender and reletting-liability dispute between a landlord and a business tenant's receivers; unrelated to lodging/boarding.

court: Lancaster County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Suit between an estranged husband and wife over rent the husband collected from a tenant on entireties property, and his right to apply it to repairs/mortgage interest; not about lodging/boarding.
Equity-jurisdiction/pleading dispute over a title-cloud bill properly certified to the law side as an ejectment action; no lodging/boarding issue.
Injunction dispute between adjoining landowners over a claimed parol-grant/prescriptive right of way (alley); unrelated to lodging.
Easement dispute over shared privy-vault sections serving four adjoining dwelling lots, resolved on implied-grant/implied-reservation doctrine; unrelated to lodging/boarding.
Criminal liquor-license case over whether an eating-house license limited to vinous/malt/brewed liquors barred sale of spirituous liquor (whiskey); unrelated to lodging/boarding regulation.
Municipal police-power case invalidating a market ordinance forbidding resale of goods bought at a public market; concerns market/commerce regulation, not lodging or boarding house licensing.
